title: Front Door Trim Ideas: Casing Styles, Exterior & Interior
h1: Front Door Trim Ideas: Exterior Trim, Casing Styles and Renter-Friendly Upgrades
description: Front door trim ideas for every home: compare casing styles, exterior trim materials, sizing, paint colors and easy apartment front door upgrades for renters.
excerpt: Compare craftsman, colonial, modern and Greek revival casing, choose exterior trim materials and colors, and upgrade an apartment front door as a renter.
image_alt: Front door trim ideas shown on a dark front door framed by wide white craftsman casing
key_takeaways: Match the casing style (craftsman, colonial, modern flat, Greek revival) to your home's architecture.
Wider casing, 3.5 in. or more, looks more custom than 2.25 in. builder trim.
PVC and composite exterior trim resist rot; prime cut ends and flash the head piece.
Semi-gloss or satin paint shows off trim profiles and wipes clean.
Renters can paint the inside of the door with permission, add peel-and-stick molding, swap hardware and add lighting.

faq.q: What is the best trim for around a front door?
faq.a: For exterior front doors, PVC or composite trim is the most durable because it won't rot, and it takes paint well. Choose a style that suits your home, such as flat craftsman casing for bungalows, pilasters and a pediment for colonial homes, or slim square trim for modern houses. Wide trim generally looks more substantial.

faq.q: How wide should door casing be?
faq.a: Most interior door casing is 2.25 to 3.5 inches wide, and 3.5 inches or more looks more custom. Craftsman and Greek revival styles often use 4.5 to 6 inches, especially with high ceilings. Exterior trim usually runs wider than interior casing. Check that you have enough wall space beside the door before choosing very wide casing.

faq.q: What color should front door trim be?
faq.a: White trim with a dark door is the classic choice and works on most homes. For a modern look, paint the trim the same color as the siding or walls so the door stands out. Painting the door and trim one deep color, like navy or green, looks rich. Use a semi-gloss or satin finish.

faq.q: How can I upgrade my apartment front door as a renter?
faq.a: With permission, paint the inside face of the door and casing. Otherwise, add removable peel-and-stick panel molding, swap the interior lever and door stop for a new finish, add a full-length mirror, a quality door mat and a plug-in sconce or lamp. Keep original parts and don't alter the lock, closer or fire rating.

faq.q: What are the different door casing styles?
faq.a: Common door casing styles include craftsman (flat sides with a heavy overhanging head), colonial (shaped ogee profile with mitered corners), modern flat (plain square boards), Greek revival (wide casings with a cornice-like head), Victorian (fluted casing with corner rosettes), Federal or Georgian (refined layered moldings) and ranch or clamshell (a simple rounded profile).
